prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from bag-drop/transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up to handoff at outbound load control; aircraft loading excluded. Elements: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit: stages bags; sends Oversize Exception Ticket to Image Resolution Desk. Bag Tag Printer: unique tags; Calibration Witness Tag (used by Maintenance Technician to verify calibration before return to service); replacement tags only after authorized confirmation. Transfer Bag Feeder: sends Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station (reconciles bag to flight, records match; Bag Match Query); no check bypass. Induction Tray Conveyor: priority admission subject to scan/spacing. Baggage Control System (Velvet): tag-flight link; screening profile; sort plan; checks identity vs routing before disposition; authorizes rejoin of assigned path after identity/flight checks; diverts unresolved bags to Secondary Inspection Chute (restricted physical exam location); receives Flight Cutoff Advisory; records disposition. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight): Recovery Route Card; induction permissive; applies routing without bypassing screening. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern): sends Flight Cutoff Advisory; flight data validating destination/service date. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel): tag read/image for identity checks. South Gate Scanner: sends Manual Rescan Receipt to Image Resolution Desk (confirms approved second image). Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper): Chute Occupancy Note; routes by destination/cutoff/status; holds bags pending manual disposition. Image Resolution Desk: presents image/exception details to operator; inconclusive image triggers physical inspection. East/West Make-Up Conveyors. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard): presents after screening; receives Carousel Release Slip from Airline Ramp Coordinator. Outbound Load Control Desk: reconciles build; confirms bag load eligibility. Actors: Operator (identity check vs tag/handling data; no uncertain matches). Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern): congestion, recovery/release authorization, disposition beyond operator authority. Explosives Response Team (Pebble): security holds/examinations; Custody Seal Log. Security Duty Manager: security release. Maintenance Technician. Airline Ramp Coordinator: confirms build readiness and flight-side constraints. Requirements: interlocks stop feed on jam/door/downstream loss; scan mismatch blocks routing; threat suspends routing until authorized disposition; unscreened bags held; flight mismatch holds bag until resolved/escalated; route/flight change requires approval before release; cutoffs include allowances.

New part:
S178: The final disposition and supporting checks are recorded so that later review can trace why the bag returned to the planned process.
S179: Safe operation depends on keeping people clear of moving equipment and maintaining a controlled path for every bag.
S180: The Baggage Operations Supervisor may stop induction when an unsafe condition, uncertain bag location, or loss of control is reported.
S181: A stop command places the affected equipment in a defined safe state without disabling unrelated routes that remain safe to operate.
S182: Before entering a conveyor or sorter hazard zone, the Maintenance Technician isolates the relevant energy sources and verifies that movement has stopped.
S183: Guards and access panels remain in place during operation, and bypasses are permitted only under an approved maintenance procedure.
S184: The Baggage Operations Supervisor uses the occupancy note to confirm that a chute can safely accept bags.
S185: The Maintenance Technician consults the Recovery Route Card before returning equipment to service after a route change.
S186: Pebble secures the response area and directs handling of any bag referred for explosives assessment.
S187: The Security Duty Manager coordinates access control when a security response affects equipment or staff movement.
S188: A scanner fault requires the affected feed to be held until the fault is assessed and the bag disposition is known.
S189: The Maintenance Technician checks for jammed bags, damaged belts, sensor obstruction, and signs of mechanical wear before clearing a fault.
S190: Lantern supplies current flight data so that operating routes can be checked against active assignments.
S191: The Baggage Control System records equipment alarms and presents the affected route for review by authorized personnel.
S192: When the Induction Tray Conveyor stops unexpectedly, staff prevent further bag entry and keep the approach area clear.
S193: The Maintenance Technician removes a jam only after confirming isolation and arranging safe access to the blockage.
S194: The Bag Reconciliation Station supports verification when a bag's location or identity is uncertain after an interruption.
S195: East Make-Up Conveyor runs only after its guards are confirmed closed and its downstream capacity is available.
S196: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is held from receiving bags when its discharge area is obstructed or its operating status is uncertain.
S197: The Maintenance Technician performs corrective work and reports any condition that prevents safe restart.
S198: The Baggage Operations Supervisor controls the operational hold, communicates its scope, and confirms that affected staff understand the restriction.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
